newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus dockworkers strike over staff cutdown.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus dockworkers strike over staff cutdown.

text.p: Dockworkers at Limassol port in Cyprus went on strike on Monday to protest management moves to cut down on staff numbers working two shifts, workers said.
Workers declared a 24-hour strike, but are threatening to make it an indefinite one if their demands concerning staffing levels are not met.
"Tomorrow (Tuesday) we will declare an indefinite strike if the Cyprus Ports Authority (CPA) remains intransigent," dockworkers representative Andreas Patalos told Cyprus radio.
Workers have complained that a decision taken by the authority to cut down on staff numbers on afternoon and evening shifts is contrary to staffing level agreements.
There was no immediate indication of how the strike was affecting work at the port.
CPA chairman Costas Erotocritou told Reuters he would be meeting union representatives later on Monday to discuss the matter. "Their action is totally unjustified," he said.
